title: Referred pain and convergence
objective: Explain referred pain via viscerosomatic convergence in the dorsal horn.

steps.title: Wires that share a line
steps.body: Visceral and somatic afferents from the same spinal level often **[[converge]]** onto the *same* [[dorsal horn]] neurons — **[[viscerosomatic convergence]]**. The brain, used to signals from skin, misreads a visceral signal as coming from the skin region sharing that line.

visual.alt: A heart afferent and a left-arm skin afferent have their cell bodies side by side in the same DRG, and both synapse onto one neuron in the T1–T4 dorsal horn. The heart afferent fires, the shared dorsal-horn neuron fires, and its signal crosses the cord and ascends to the brain. The brain lights up, and the chest wall over the heart and the left arm both glow, with one 'felt here' label pointing to each, while the arm's own afferent stays quiet.
visual.caption: Heart and arm afferents share a dorsal-horn neuron, so the brain places heart pain in the chest wall and left arm.

steps.prompt: Why is heart pain often 'felt' in the left arm (**[[referred pain]]**)?
options: Cardiac and arm afferents converge on the same dorsal-horn neurons
Pain spreads backward along the arm's sensory nerves
The vagus nerve carries heart pain down into the arm
Reduced blood flow also reaches the arm muscles
steps.explanation: Shared central wiring makes the brain mislocalize the visceral signal to the somatic territory it usually hears from — the classic referred-pain mechanism.

variants.setup: During a heart attack, cardiac pain afferents enter the upper thoracic cord (T1–T4).
variants.prompt: Besides the chest, where is the pain classically felt?
variants.reveal: Cardiac afferents share T1–T4 dorsal-horn neurons with afferents from the chest wall and inner arm, so the brain refers heart pain there.

steps.setup: A patient reports shoulder-tip pain, and it turns out the diaphragm is irritated.
options: Convergence of diaphragm and shoulder afferents centrally
The shoulder joint itself is badly torn or injured
The irritated diaphragm presses on nerves in the shoulder
steps.reveal: Diaphragm (phrenic) and shoulder afferents share central levels, so diaphragmatic irritation refers to the shoulder — the same convergence logic.

variants.prompt: Referred pain patterns are explained by…
options: Central convergence of visceral and somatic afferents
Visceral nerves branching out to supply the skin
Sensory nerves somehow conducting backward here
variants.explanation: Shared dorsal-horn targets cause the brain to mislocalize visceral signals.

steps.title: A diagnostic fingerprint
steps.body: Referred-pain maps are clinically useful: the *pattern* hints at which organ and spinal level is involved. It also warns researchers that where a signal is 'felt' isn't where it started.
